To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neurotensin, released from striatal neurons, acts at the level of the pallidal neurons, where it inhibits the N‐type calcium current.
NT, likely from striatal terminals, affects N‐type Ca2+ channels in the lateral aspects, and in about 56%, of GP neurons, and that this effect is mediated by the postsynaptic NT1.
NT, likely originating from the striatal afferents, is able to modulate the activity of the GP neurons, by means of the activation of NTS1 receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neurotensin receptor NTS1 in the globus pallidius (GP).
the study of the effects of neurotensin in the globus pallidum.
the role of the neuropeptide neurotensins (NT) in the regulation of dopamine (DA)-mediated functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NT is not only a presynaptic neuromodulator, but it can also be a postsynaptic neuromediator.
the effects of NT on N‐type Ca2+ channels are mediated by the NT1 receptor and that the NT1 is present on about 50–56% of the GP neurons.
neurotensin has a significant impact on N‐type Ca2+ current among pallidal neurons, and this is a novel finding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NT acts as a “neuromodulator” of GP neurons, and that the NT‐mediated effects are likely to involve a complex interaction between NTS1 and D2 dopamine receptors, and possibly other receptors.
NT is an important modulator of GP neurons and that NT receptors are widely expressed in the pallidal neurons.
the neurotensinergic system, in addition to a role of “excitatory” modulation of pallidal neurons, may also affect calcium currents, which may have an impact on the pallidal firing pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuropeptide NT, released from striatal neurons, can modulate the firing pattern of GP neurons through the postsynaptically expressed receptor NTS1, which is present in the majority of neurons in both sub‐populations.
neurotensin is a modulator of calcium currents in globus pallidum neurons.
NT has an important role in the GP.
